content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work can lose formulas, formatting, and auditability. This skill guides Excel creation, editing, recalculation, and validation with openpyxl, pandas, and clear modeling standards.
actual_capabilities: Create Excel workbooks with formulas using openpyxl examples.
Edit worksheets, insert rows, delete columns, and add sheets.
Apply color conventions for inputs, formulas, links, and external references.
Set number formats for currency, percentages, multiples, and year labels.
Read workbook data with pandas or openpyxl while preserving formulas when needed.
Use checklists for formula references, error checks, and recalculation review.
limitations: It does not include a recalc.py implementation.
openpyxl can write formulas but cannot calculate formula results.
It focuses on .xlsx workflows, not Google Sheets APIs.
It provides guidance and examples, not a full spreadsheet application.

use_cases.title: Build a Financial Model
use_cases.description: Create a workbook with assumptions, formulas, color standards, and readable number formats.

use_cases.title: Prepare Data Workbooks
use_cases.description: Read Excel files, inspect sheets, and preserve formulas during analysis or edits.

use_cases.title: Validate Spreadsheet Outputs
use_cases.description: Check formulas, cross-sheet references, and common Excel errors before sharing a workbook.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook for my revenue plan. Use formulas for totals, format currency values, and mark input cells clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Read Workbook Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this .xlsx file and decide when to use pandas or openpyxl. Summarize useful sheets and preserve formulas where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the workbook by adding a scenario sheet, linking it to the data sheet, and applying currency and percentage formats.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Formula Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect workbook formulas, map cross-sheet references, run available recalculation checks, and report #REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, and #NAME? issues.

output_examples.input: Create a three-year revenue workbook with growth assumptions.
output: Workbook includes separate assumption, calculation, and summary areas.
Inputs are visually marked and totals remain formula driven.
Currency and percentage formats are applied consistently.

output_examples.input: Review an existing spreadsheet for formula problems.
output: Formula cells, linked sheets, and potential reference issues are summarized.
Common Excel errors are listed with suggested fixes.
The review explains where recalculation is required.

output_examples.input: Edit a workbook without losing formulas.
output: The workbook is opened in a mode that preserves formulas.
Requested rows, columns, and sheets are changed carefully.
Final checks confirm key formulas and formats remain intact.

best_practices: Keep assumptions as input cells and calculations as formula cells.
Preserve formulas unless the user asks for static values.
Validate references and spreadsheet errors before sharing the final workbook.
anti_patterns: Do not replace formulas with calculated values when the workbook must stay auditable.
Do not save a data-only workbook when formulas must be preserved.
Do not assume fiscal year columns without confirming the column map.

faq.question: Can this skill create .xlsx files?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides openpyxl patterns for creating workbooks, formulas, sheets, formatting, and saved Excel files.

faq.question: Can it edit existing Excel files?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to load a workbook, update cells, add sheets, and preserve formulas.

faq.question: Does it calculate Excel formula results?
faq.answer: No. openpyxl writes formulas but does not calculate results. Use a spreadsheet engine or verified recalculation helper.

faq.question: Does it support financial modeling standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents color conventions, number formats, formula checks, and common modeling pitfalls.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it include spreadsheet security scanning?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on workbook construction and validation, not malware scanning or macro analysis.
